# Fairpractice Capitation (`fairpractice-capitation`)

Reconciles capitation payments with your member roster month by month: eligible members not paid, members paid at the wrong rate or twice, payments for members not eligible, and retroactive adds and terms, with the amount to dispute and the amount to set aside for recoupment. Member names and IDs are masked before results reach the model.

**Fairpractice Capitation never sends disputes to a plan. Fairpractice Capitation never sends refunds or payments.**

Fairpractice ver 1 · Care management and value-based care · MIT · Node 20 or newer · local files only · patient and staff identifiers masked before results reach the model · built on [`fairpractice-core`](../fairpractice-core)

```bash
npx -y fairpractice-capitation demo
npx -y fairpractice-capitation mcp --root ./practice-files
```

## What the sample data shows

Fictional data only: a made-up practice, plan and members. Any likeness to real people is chance.

- [`member-roster.csv`](fixtures/member-roster.csv) and [`cap-payments.csv`](fixtures/cap-payments.csv) for August to October 2026. Planted:
  - Ben Cole: October paid at the Adult rate (32) instead of Senior (55).
  - Cleo Dunn: September not paid.
  - Dev Ernst: termed August 31 but paid for September and October.
  - Eve Ford: October paid twice.
  - Finn Gale: effective August 1, first paid on October 5 for August and September (retro adds).
  - Gus Hale: termed August 31; September paid, then taken back on October 5 (retro term, nets to zero).
- [`settings.json`](fixtures/settings.json): example rates by category. [`settings-typo.json`](fixtures/settings-typo.json) misspells a setting and is refused.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does | Policy |
|---|---|---|
| `capitation_check` | List members not paid, wrong rates, duplicates, payments for members not eligible, and retro adds and terms, with the net to dispute. | runs |
| `capitation_write_report` | Write capitation.csv (one row per item, with blank owner and decision columns) and capitation.html into out_dir (default fairpractice-out/capitation). | runs |
| `capitation_recall` | Search this agent's own memory of the customer's setup: accepted facts (in use) and facts waiting for a person. | runs |
| `capitation_learn` | Propose one fact about the customer's setup for this agent to remember. | runs |
| `capitation_accept_learning` | A named person accepts or rejects a fact waiting in this agent's memory. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `capitation_retire_memory` | A named person stops an accepted fact from applying. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `dispute_submit` | Fairpractice Capitation never sends disputes to a plan. | refused |
| `refund_send` | Fairpractice Capitation never sends refunds or payments. | refused |

Any tool name not in this table is blocked, including names a model invents. Refused tools are listed so a model can see they exist and are refused.

### `capitation_check` arguments

| Argument | What it is |
|---|---|
| `roster` (required) | Your member roster under --root: member ID, name, effective and term dates, rate category or rate |
| `payments` (required) | Capitation payment detail: member ID, coverage month, amount (negative for takebacks), paid date |
| `settings` | Optional settings JSON: rates, tolerance |
| `from` | First month to check, YYYY-MM; default the first month paid |
| `to` | Last month to check, YYYY-MM; default the last month paid |
| `status` | Only items with this status |
| `limit` | Most items to return to the model (the report file always has all of them) |

## Columns it reads

Tables can be CSV, TSV, semicolon- or pipe-separated text, Excel `.xlsx`, JSON or JSONL. Columns are matched by the names below (any case and punctuation), and by their usual names in German, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Japanese, Chinese and Korean. Dates become `YYYY-MM-DD`. Columns marked *masked* hold patient or staff identifiers.

The PointClickCare, MatrixCare and American HealthTech style names were written from public help pages and general knowledge, **not checked against real exports**. Run `npx fairpractice-capitation inspect <file>` (column names and shapes only, never values) and name any column it misses in `remedy-sources.json`.

### Member roster (`roster`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `member_id` (required) | text (masked) | Member ID, Member #, Subscriber ID, Insurance ID, Medicaid ID, Beneficiary ID |
| `patient_name` | text (masked) | Patient, Patient Name, Name, Client, Client Name, Member, Member Name, Beneficiary |
| `effective` | date | Effective, Effective Date, Eff Date, Start, Start Date, Assigned |
| `term` | date | Term, Term Date, End, End Date, Disenrolled |
| `category` | text | Rate Category, Category, Aid Category, Rate Cell, Age Band, Product |
| `rate` | amount | Rate, PMPM, Expected PMPM, Cap Rate |

### Capitation payments (`payments`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `member_id` (required) | text (masked) | Member ID, Member #, Subscriber ID, Insurance ID, Medicaid ID, Beneficiary ID |
| `patient_name` | text (masked) | Patient, Patient Name, Name, Client, Client Name, Member, Member Name, Beneficiary |
| `month` (required) | text | Coverage Month, Month, Service Month, Eligibility Month, Period |
| `amount` (required) | amount | Amount, Cap Amount, Payment, Paid, Net Amount |
| `paid_date` | date | Paid Date, Payment Date, Check Date, Run Date |

## Settings file (`capitation_settings`)

A small JSON file you pass by path. A misspelled setting is refused by name rather than ignored, so a typo never silently changes a check.

| Setting | What it does |
|---|---|
| `rates` | Expected monthly rate by rate category, when the roster has no rate column |
| `tolerance` | Difference ignored as rounding; default 0.01 |

## Memory

`capitation_learn` only proposes a fact; nothing changes until a named person accepts it with `capitation_accept_learning`, which is one click even in Auto. Facts live in a hash-chained file under `.remedy/memory/`; if the chain does not verify, no fact is used. Credentials, personal identifiers and text that reads like instructions to an AI are refused.

| Kind | What an accepted fact does |
|---|---|

## Install

Node 20 or newer. No other runtime dependencies besides `fairpractice-core` and `fairclaim-core`.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "fairpractice-capitation": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "fairpractice-capitation",
        "mcp",
        "--root",
        "/path/to/practice-files"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Claude Code: `claude mcp add fairpractice-capitation -- npx -y fairpractice-capitation mcp --root .`, or use the plugin files in this folder.

## CLI

```bash
fairpractice-capitation tools                 # every tool, its policy and arguments
fairpractice-capitation sources               # the columns each input is read from
fairpractice-capitation inspect <file>        # how a file would be read (names and shapes, never values)
fairpractice-capitation call capitation_check '{"roster":"<roster>","payments":"<payments>"}'
fairpractice-capitation eval                  # the private eval cases on the fictional fixtures
fairpractice-capitation demo
```

## Patient and staff data

Results go to an AI model, so identifiers are masked before they leave the agent: patient and staff names become stable pseudonyms such as `PT-3f9a1c2e`, record and account numbers become `MRN-…` or `ACCT-…`, and e-mails and phone numbers are removed, also inside free text. Report files written to disk keep real names because staff work from them: keep them in a folder only your staff can open. The shared tests check that no fictional identifier from the fixtures reaches any eval result, and the hostile-input check plants spreadsheet formulas, HTML and AI-aimed instructions in the data. This keeps PHI away from the model; it is **not** a HIPAA compliance determination. Your business associate agreements, access controls and policies still apply.

## Limits

- Reads only the files you give it. It does not log in to an EHR, practice-management system, payer portal, clearinghouse, state system, HR or payroll system, or bank.
- Payer, Medicare, Medicaid, state and federal rules are summarised from public material as of 2026, and the numbers are settings you supply; a billing, compliance or legal professional checks them before you rely on them.
- Not legal, billing, coding, tax, clinical or HIPAA advice. It does not diagnose or recommend care. A person decides what to bill, pay, report, file or send.
- Every call is written to a hash-chained audit log under `.remedy/` in the root. No network calls, no telemetry, no credentials. The bundled data is fictional.
